name: scalar-writers
what: time of one call of the escape of one context (xml, json, js, css, troff) for one value, in a loop over a list of 64 values that moves the output position by the count, as a render does; ns per value
purpose_in_the_task_list: Task c08c8baf (the escape and its room), plan A4, commit 5: the five scalar writers are measured before and after on the escape alone, because workloads 1 to 3 of bench/render.cpp are html only. The form that is not slower than the arm before beyond the noise in every build enters include/
method: not the method of mbedded-cbor/bench/README.md: one run, 6 rounds, the arm order alternates by round (forward, then reversed), each process 5 repetitions of 2^22 input bytes for each input, timed with std::chrono::steady_clock; arm 1 is arm 0 built twice; sysbench cpu 10 times for 1 s before the first round; each arm is held to the bytes of arm 0 before it is timed (every byte value alone and beside a letter, 16 pieces of js and troff at every position of every length 0 to 20, and every value of the inputs), with a room of escaped_size_max_in(context, n) + 32 bytes and guard bytes behind it; no gate, no steal

arms.0: the writers of include/mustache/escape.hpp at 4dac08e: a branch for each escaped byte, std::ranges::copy of each escape, a store of one byte for each plain byte
arms.1: the same code as arm 0, a second binary: the noise of the cell
arms.2: each piece of output, a plain byte too, is one 8-byte word stored through std::span<char, 8>, std::bit_cast and std::copy_n, and the count moves on by the length of the piece; the word of each byte comes from a table of 256 words for each context, built at compile time; js tests the first byte of U+2028 and U+2029 and then starts_with; troff writes the first and the last place of a line apart from the table
arms.3: arm 2 with each run of plain bytes copied with std::copy_n into the room (found with std::find_if over the same tables) and only the escaped bytes stored as words

inputs.<n>-<p>: 64 values of n bytes (16, 64, 1024) from letters, digits and a space; each byte is a mark of the context with the probability p percent (0 or 5); marks: xml &<>"', json " \ line feed and 0x01, js ' < \ /, css ' } < \, troff \ " ' ` ~ ^; fixed seed
inputs.lines-<n>-<p>: troff only: the same with a line feed at every 16th byte

builds: g++-16 and clang++-23, -O2 and -Os, -march=x86-64-v3; -std=c++26 -DNDEBUG -Wall -Wextra -Werror -falign-functions=64 -falign-loops=64 (g++ also -falign-jumps=64) -DARM=<arm>; one binary for each arm and build
headers: none (probe.cpp holds a copy of the writers of 4dac08e and the forms of arms 2 and 3)
